name: Abigail
description: David's wife living at the time of United Monarchy

points: There was a very great man in Maon whose possessions were in Carmel, three thousand sheep and a thousand goats, shearing his sheep in Carmel. His name was Nabal, and his wife was Abigail, a woman of good understanding and of a beautiful countenance; but the man was churlish and evil in his doings, and he was of the house of Caleb.

note.label: 1 Samuel 25: Nabal's Folly and Abigail's Wisdom

points: One of the young men told Abigail: David sent messengers out of the wilderness to salute our master, and he railed on them. But the men were very good unto us; we were not hurt, neither missed we any thing as long as we were conversant with them; they were a wall unto us both by night and day while we were keeping the sheep. David's men had been giving Nabal's shepherds protection from their enemies.

note.label: 1 Samuel 25: Nabal's Folly and Abigail's Wisdom

points: Abigail made haste and took two hundred loaves, two bottles of wine, five sheep ready dressed, parched corn, clusters of raisins, and cakes of figs, laid them on asses, and sent her servants on before her; but she told not her husband Nabal.

note.label: 1 Samuel 25: Nabal's Folly and Abigail's Wisdom

points: When Abigail saw David she hasted, lighted off the ass, fell at his feet, and said, Upon me, my lord, upon me let this iniquity be. She was not the one who did anything wrong, but she took that iniquity upon herself; she was being that pillar of her house, using wisdom to protect it, for the scripture says she was a woman of good understanding.

note.label: 1 Samuel 25: Nabal's Folly and Abigail's Wisdom

points: And David said to Abigail, Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, which sent thee this day to meet me. Wait — his what? I thought the woman had to be shut up and she cannot give any advice.

note.label: SHE REVERENCE HER HUSBAND: Submission, Grace & Self-Examination of a Biblical Wife

points: Abigail came home and Nabal held a feast in his house like the feast of a king, and his heart was merry within him, for he was very drunken; so she told him nothing, less or more, until the morning light.

note.label: 1 Samuel 25: Nabal's Folly and Abigail's Wisdom

points: When David heard that Nabal was dead, he said, Blessed be the Lord, that hath pleaded the cause of my reproach from the hand of Nabal, and hath kept his servant from evil: for the Lord hath returned the wickedness of Nabal upon his own head. Then David sent and communed with Abigail, to take her to him to wife.

note.label: 1 Samuel 25: Nabal's Folly and Abigail's Wisdom

points: David passed over with the six hundred men that were with him unto Achish the son of Maoch, king of Gath, every man with his household, David with his two wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess and Abigail the Carmelitess, Nabal's wife. When it was told Saul that David was fled to Gath, he sought no more again for him.

note.label: 1 Samuel 27: David Dwells in the Land of the Philistines

points: David went up with his two wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess and Abigail the widow of Nabal the Carmelite, and with every man and his household, and they dwelt in the cities of Hebron.

note.label: 2 Samuel 2: David Anointed King Over Judah

points: Sons were born to David in Hebron: the firstborn Amnon of Ahinoam, Chileab of Abigail, Absalom the son of Maachah the daughter of the king of Geshur, Adonijah the son of Haggith, Shephatiah of Abital, and Ithream of Eglah his wife.

note.label: 2 Samuel 3: The House of David Waxes Stronger
